title: Projections from a finite inverse limit are surjective
statement: Let $I$ be a preordered set in which every pair has a common upper bound (a directed preordered set), and let $(S_i,p_{ji})$ be an inverse system indexed by $I$: each $S_i$ is a finite nonempty set [lem-galois-axioms] and for $j\ge i$ there is a transition map $p_{ji}:S_j\to S_i$, compatible with identities and compositions. Assume every $p_{ji}$ is surjective. Then the inverse limit $S=\varprojlim_i S_i$ is nonempty and each projection $S\to S_i$ is surjective.

mathlib_match.how: Two declarations, one per clause. Encode the inverse system over the directed preordered set I as a functor S : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Type. `nonempty_sections_of_finite_inverse_system` (lines 111-113, with J = I, [Preorder I] [IsDirectedOrder I]) gives a compatible section, hence the inverse limit is nonempty; `CategoryTheory.Functor.eval_section_surjective_of_surjective` (lines 304-322, theorem at 312, with J = Iᵒᵖ, which is cofiltered-or-empty since I is directed) gives surjectivity of evaluation at every index. Finite and nonempty values and surjective transition maps are exactly the hypotheses of these declarations, and sections/evaluation are the inverse limit and its projections.
